questions.question: "Sclerosing Adenosis" is a component of fibrocystic change that can mimic cancer because it often presents with:
choices: Clusters of amorphous or pleomorphic calcifications
questions.detail: This benign proliferative condition is a common cause of false-positive biopsies for calcifications.

questions.question: "Acute Mastitis" is most common in which population?
questions.detail: Bacteria enter through nipple cracks during breastfeeding.

questions.question: A breast "Abscess" is best diagnosed and followed using which modality?
questions.detail: Ultrasound identifies the fluid collection and can guide therapeutic drainage.

questions.question: "Fibrocystic Changes" (FCC) is a broad term. Which of the following is NOT a typical feature of FCC?
questions.detail: FCC is a benign process; spiculated masses are suspicious for cancer.

questions.question: "Plasma Cell Mastitis" (Secretory disease) is characterized by which pathognomonic finding?
questions.detail: These are benign BI-RADS 2 findings seen in older women.
